summary: A first-person narrator is held in a remote forest laboratory where a doctor, who has performed a sperm extraction procedure on a comatose man named Steve, justifies harvesting women's ova and embryonic material. The doctor claims he is returning to the women what was taken from them and that their children are sacred miracles linked to the deity Kukulkan. The narrator, hallucinating and seething with anger, calls him a criminal before he leaves and shuts the door.
one_line: A captive narrator confronts a laboratory doctor who justifies stealing women's ova and sperm as sacred acts tied to Kukulkan.
key_facts: The doctor says that, given Steve's condition, he chose the simplest procedure: a small incision in the vas deferens to extract a substantial quantity of motile sperm.
The doctor says he had performed the same procedure before on a Swedish tourist who was in a car accident up by Lake Atitlan and lay in a coma in Guatemala City for weeks.
The narrator thinks Kevin and Rachel look Nordic, big and blond, and believes the Swede must have been their father.
The narrator accuses the doctor of stealing her ova and Sarah's, and of bringing other women to the laboratory.
The doctor says he has ample leftover embryonic material for research, implying the women's ova are not used for research.
The narrator remembers the frightened eyes of the women upstairs and feels herself seething with anger.
The doctor calls himself a criminal's opposite, saying he is giving the women back a small part of what people like them had taken away.
The doctor claims he provides living proof that the women's truths are still powerful.
The doctor says women come to him for a blessing when they hope to bear a child, and that he can cause their first child to be a descendant of the white deity Kukulkan.
The doctor quotes a great philosopher: 'All religions are true.' and asks who are they to judge.
The doctor says the patterns women weave on fabrics in Baalum match the designs on a thousand-year-old pyramid that had been buried and lost to them.
The doctor describes the women's symbols as a road map of their unseen world, where gods rule lightning bolts and the germination of corn.
The doctor says the special infants who come are miracles that must be returned, and that the women now wish the narrator to be part of that.
The doctor closes the door with a slam and a hard click as he leaves, while the narrator's hallucinations swirl around her.
